clue.text: If neat MS is sent round, all should be clear

indicators.note: letters sent round in a whirl are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Once a tidy manuscript has been circulated, everyone should understand the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is sent round' signals the rearrangement; 'all should be' merely joins wordplay to the definition, which reads as though everything will become clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something manifest is obvious and plain to see, a synonym of clear.

clue.text: It's sticky on reflection eg about mid-July

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the whole assembly is read backwards
eg goes about, that is around, the other letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: mid- asks for the central letters of the month's name

explanation.surface: A sticky substance found, thinking it over, around the middle of July.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the July centre inside EG to make EULG, and 'on reflection' turns the whole thing round; 'It's sticky' is the definition, not a description of July weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue is an adhesive, the stuff described as sticky.

clue.text: Notice to merge to come next?

parts.note: a notice in a paper is an ad, short for advertisement
to merge is to join

explanation.surface: A memo announcing a corporate merger as the next step.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjoin is to lie next to or border on something, so to come next to it.

clue.text: Forced to act with a politician, the Spanish and French having departed

parts.note: a means one, the Roman numeral I
MP, Member of Parliament
el is Spanish for the
le is French for the, sharing the previous the
d is the abbreviation for departed in timetables

explanation.surface: Someone pushed into action alongside a politician once foreign visitors have left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Spanish and French' gives two articles: EL and LE; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be impelled is to be driven or compelled to do something, i.e. forced to act.

clue.text: Property of 2 showing tendency not to leave

definitions.meaning: 2-down's answer is an adhesive, whose defining property is clinging
a guest who lingers too long has this quality

explanation.definitionFit: Stickiness is adhesiveness, and informally the tendency of a person to linger and not go.

clue.text: Carried round the island

parts.note: borne is the past participle of bear, to carry
O is round in shape

explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is a large island in South-East Asia shared by three countries.

clue.text: 8 ad replaced by a Poet Laureate on parliamentary business

indicators.note: the letters are placed afresh in a different order

parts.note: the answer to 8-down, meaning on a regular basis
Andrew Motion was the UK Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009

explanation.surface: An annual advert supplanted by a royal poet working on parliamentary affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges YEARLY plus AD into EARLYDAY. An early day motion is a House of Commons motion that is rarely debated.
explanation.definitionFit: An early day motion is a formal item tabled in the UK House of Commons, a piece of parliamentary business.

clue.text: Aristocrat is surrounded by unknowns on a regular basis

indicators.note: the aristocrat sits with letters placed on either side of him

parts.note: y is an algebraic unknown, so two of them give YY
an earl is a British nobleman

explanation.surface: A nobleman routinely surrounded by strangers.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearly means happening every year, a regular recurrence.

clue.text: See 7
Punishment that's fair

definitions.meaning: as in weather that is pleasant and dry

explanation.definitionFit: A fine is a monetary penalty, and fine weather is fair weather.

clue.text: Pastel once restored, showing many different colours

indicators.note: something restored has been reworked, so the letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A pastel picture, once restored, displays a rainbow of hues.
explanation.definitionFit: Opalescent describes a milky iridescence like an opal, showing shifting colours.

clue.text: Falcon of the yellowhammer/linnet family

indicators.note: the answer is formed of letters drawn from inside the two bird names

explanation.surface: A bird of prey said to belong to the same family as two finches.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the join of yellowhamMER/LINnet; the bird family surface is false, as a merlin is a falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: The merlin is a small falcon found across the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: Army officer who might be capped shortly, say

definitions.text: Army officer who might be capped shortly, say

parts.words: Army officer who might be capped shortly, say
parts.note: this officer's rank is shortened to Lt, written with a capital, so shortly he is capped

explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a junior commissioned officer in the army, abbreviated Lt.

clue.text: Sweet noted for 5?

parts.note: a sweet on a stick known for its tackiness; noted also hints at the famous pop song of the same name

explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard sweet on a stick, which is often sticky.

clue.text: Test outside aim with it

indicators.note: the word for test goes outside, around, the word for aim

parts.note: to try is to test
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Testing whether one's goal is fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: With it is slang for fashionable, as is trendy.

clue.text: I err, made drunk and getting more vague

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An admission that drinking makes one fuzzier.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamier means more dreamlike and hazy, a comparative of vague.

clue.text: Draw attention to notice

definitions.meaning: to ... to something is to refer to it
an advertisement, especially in short form

explanation.definitionFit: Advert as a verb means to refer to, and as a noun it is a short form of advertisement.

clue.text: Rattle on about patient

indicators.note: about here means in a confused order, all around

explanation.surface: A chatterer rambles on about someone in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerant means able to bear things calmly, a close synonym of patient.

clue.text: Drink and where to get it on account?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after

parts.note: drink is served in bars

explanation.surface: A drink, and where to buy it on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: BARSAC is a sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet dessert wine from a commune in Bordeaux, so a drink.

clue.text: The man's confused with a front and back — it's an abomination

indicators.note: one A goes at the front and one at the back, enclosing the rest

parts.note: taken as written, used at both ends

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A man who is muddled is called a horror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' gives NATHEM, and 'front and back' places it between two copies of A; the man's possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is something or someone loathed, an object of abomination.

clue.text: Unspoilt countryside in essence

definitions.meaning: the natural world untouched by people
the basic character of something, as in in essence

explanation.definitionFit: Nature means the wild natural world and also the inherent character of a thing.

clue.text: Outcome of set rule endlessly applied

indicators.note: applied suggests the letters are put to work in a new arrangement
endlessly drops the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: What follows when a fixed regulation is enforced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts RULE to RUL; 'applied' rearranges SET plus RUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is the consequence or outcome of something.

clue.text: Fly but without a place to land

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to fly is to flee, run away

explanation.surface: Flying, but with nowhere to touch down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link; 'without' removes one A from RUNAWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is the strip on an airfield where aircraft land and take off.

clue.text: I cut out the hard stuff when at work

definitions.text: I cut out the hard stuff when at work

parts.words: I cut out the hard stuff when at work
parts.note: reads like a reformed drinker, but describes a tradesman shaping hard rock on the job

explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason is a craftsman who cuts and dresses stone for building.

clue.text: Plant's found right in the middle of the bog

indicators.note: the letter for right is set in the middle of the word for bog

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land

explanation.surface: A plant growing in the centre of a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is a flowerless plant with feathery fronds.

clue.text: Two notes about morning glory

indicators.note: the two notes go about, around, the morning

parts.note: F and E are musical notes
am, ante meridiem, is morning

explanation.surface: A couple of musical notes about the morning glory flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the flower morning glory, but 'morning' is AM and 'glory' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame is renown, and glory means great fame or honour.

clue.text: Attractive photos reportedly first of a fairy-tale character

indicators.note: first places the photos part before the attractive part
reportedly means as said aloud, a word sounding like another

parts.note: photographic prints
charming means attractive

explanation.surface: Glamorous photos of a storybook hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Charming is the handsome hero of fairy tales such as Cinderella.

clue.text: See 25
